rules.when: The task is a separate read-only planning assignment: architecture, decomposition, acceptance criteria, or a design decision needed before implementation. It is not routine task coordination or implementation from an accepted plan.
rules.why: High reasoning belongs in bounded planning. Return a concise plan and stop before implementation.

rules.when: The task is narrow read-only reconnaissance, file gathering, a mechanical edit, formatting, a targeted rename, or another straightforward operation with clear acceptance criteria.
rules.why: Keep the highest-volume routine work on explicit low-reasoning profiles whose live account probes passed.

rules.when: The task is scoped implementation or straightforward tests from a sufficiently clear accepted plan, without unresolved architecture or a previous inadequate low-tier attempt.
rules.why: Execution starts at low reasoning after planning has removed ambiguity. Choose among subscriptions using current quota evidence.

rules.when: The task is an additional independent review explicitly requested or justified by the change, ambiguous debugging, or implementation that the manager has explicitly escalated after a low-tier attempt was inadequate. Routine acceptance code review is performed by the medium-reasoning manager itself and is not a worker assignment. Unresolved architectural planning decisions belong to the planning rule.
rules.why: Use medium reasoning for an additional review or a demonstrated need. An extra reviewer assists rather than replaces the manager's personal code review; return architectural uncertainty to the high-tier planner.
